questions.question: A 32-year-old woman presents with refractory hypertension and an abdominal bruit heard over the right flank. Renal angiography demonstrates a characteristic 'string of beads' appearance of the right renal artery. Which of the following histopathological findings is most commonly associated with this patient's underlying condition?
options: Medial fibroplasia with alternating thick and thin muscular layers
Intimal atheromatous plaque formation with fibrous capping
Transmural necrotizing vasculitis with fibrinoid necrosis
Hyaline arteriolosclerosis of afferent renal arterioles

questions.question: A 22-year-old woman presents for a routine physical exam. She notes mild scleral icterus during periods of physical stress or fasting, but is otherwise asymptomatic. Laboratory studies reveal an isolated elevated total bilirubin of 2.9 mg/dL with a direct bilirubin of 0.3 mg/dL. Transaminases, alkaline phosphatase, and hemoglobin are within normal limits. Which mechanism best accounts for this presentation?
options: Deficiency of the canalicular multidrug resistance-associated protein 2 (MRP2)
Mutation in the promoter region of the UGT1A1 gene leading to reduced glucuronidation
Complete genetic absence of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity
Autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic interlobular bile ducts

questions.question: A 65-year-old man in the postoperative unit following total knee arthroplasty has been receiving subcutaneous unfractionated heparin for thromboprophylaxis. On postoperative day 6, his platelet count decreases from a baseline of 240,000/µL to 90,000/µL. Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) is suspected. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate step in management?
options: Discontinue unfractionated heparin and switch to low-molecular-weight heparin
Administer a platelet transfusion immediately to prevent major bleeding
Discontinue heparin and initiate a direct thrombin inhibitor such as argatroban
Discontinue heparin and immediately initiate loading doses of oral warfarin

questions.question: A 45-year-old man with a history of intravenous drug use presents to the emergency department with high fever, chills, and pleuritic chest pain. Physical examination reveals a holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border that increases in intensity with inspiration, along with splinter hemorrhages under his fingernails. Which organism is the most likely cause of this patient's acute illness?
options: Streptococcus viridans
Enterococcus faecalis
Streptococcus gallolyticus
Staphylococcus aureus

questions.question: A 70-year-old man presents with acute, severe pain and swelling in his right knee. Arthrocentesis yields cloudy synovial fluid with 28,000 WBCs/µL (85% neutrophils). Compensated polarized light microscopy reveals weakly positive birefringent, rhomboid-shaped crystals within the synovial fluid. Which of the following is the chemical composition of these crystals?
options: Monosodium urate
Calcium pyrophosphate
Calcium oxalate
Basic calcium phosphate
